title: Stop the tracer from keeping finished requests

blocks.text: The checkout service traces every request: `SpanTable` keeps a span per request object, and the web layer calls `event(request, ...)` while it handles it. Since the tracer went in, the heap grows by a request body for every request served, and a heap dump shows finished requests still reachable from the tracer. An exporter also keeps finished spans for a while, to send them in batches, and needs their labels then.
`SpanTable` already records events and labels spans. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/SpanTable.java`:

items: `newTable()`: the map from each request to its span;
`open(request)`: a new span labelled `"<method> <path>"`, for example `"POST /orders"`.

blocks.text: When you're done, the tracer holds a span for as long as the web layer holds its request, and not after; a span the exporter still holds gives its label without keeping its request in memory. About four lines in total.
The tests ask the JVM for collections with `System.gc()` and wait, up to ten seconds, for a finished request to be collected.

cases.says: each request gets one span that collects its events and is labelled with its method and path
a request the web layer still holds keeps its span through collections
once nothing outside the tracer holds a request, a collection frees it and its span leaves the table
a span held after its request ends still gives its label, and does not keep the request reachable

origin.section: A WeakHashMap Entry Goes Only When Nothing Else Reaches Its Key

concepts: A WeakHashMap entry goes only when nothing else reaches its key; a value that refers to its key, or an interned literal key, keeps the entry.
